finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and saves it, so any user can set privileged or internal fields (e.g. role, isAdmin, id, email verification status, permissions) on their own account, leading to privilege escalation or account tampering. The sibling route /me/profile at line 10-12 whitelists displayName and bio, which shows the intended pattern and that /me departs from it.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled JSON body of an authenticated PUT /me request (req.body)
finding.sink: Object.assign(req.user, req.body) followed by req.store.save(req.user) persisting arbitrary attributes

trace.note: Route handler for PUT /me receives the request
Object.assign merges all req.body keys into req.user with no allowlist
req.store.save persists the modified user, including injected fields
Updated user is echoed back, confirming the change

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist or schema validation in this file. Only one source file exists, so authentication middleware that populates req.user is not visible; it would not prevent this, since the attacker is an ordinary authenticated user modifying their own record. The /me/profile route destructures only displayName and bio, so it is not affected.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 does Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist and users.js:6 saves it, while the sibling route at users.js:11-12 whitelists displayName and bio, so any authenticated user can set arbitrary fields on their own record.
